title: Open direct image Tor bound over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small étale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and $e\ge0$ an integer. Let $L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Suppose $R^qj_*F=0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] for every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $q>e$. Suppose also that, for every finite $A$-module $M$, the natural projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] for the derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]
$$ (Rj_*L)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_T\longrightarrow Rj_*(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_V) $$
is an isomorphism, where $M_S$ denotes the constant module sheaf on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Then $Rj_*L$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+e]$, tested against every $A_T$-module sheaf.

source.place: Step 3, passage from finite constant-module Tor tests for Rj_* L to all module sheaves by stalks and filtered unions.

proof.text: Put $Q=Rj_*L$. For a finite $A$-module $M$ set $E_M=L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_V$. The constant sheaf $M_V$ is one of the degree-zero sheaves allowed in the Tor-amplitude hypothesis. Thus $\mathcal H^r(E_M)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. In particular $E_M$ is bounded below, even though finite $A$-modules need not have finite projective dimension.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude (1), applied to the constant module sheaf

proof.text: The category of $A$-module sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ has enough injectives. Since $E_M$ has no cohomology below $a$, choose an injective representative $I_M$ with $I_M^r=0$ for $r<a$. The bounded-below derived-functor computation gives $Rj_*E_M\cong Q_T(j_*I_M)$, where $Q_T$ is localization from complexes to the derived category, not the object $Q$. Additivity of $j_*$ gives $j_*0=0$, so this representing complex is zero below $a$. Consequently $\mathcal H^r(Rj_*E_M)=0$ for $r<a$.

Apply the finite-cohomological-dimension derived upper-bound lemma to $F=j_*:\operatorname{Mod}(A_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$, $N=e$, $t=b$, and $E=E_M$. Its abelian-category and enough-injectives hypotheses hold for these module-sheaf categories; $j_*$ is additive and left exact, $e\ge0$, and the required vanishing $R^qj_*F'=0$ for every module sheaf $F'$ and $q>e$ is precisely the hypothesis of the item. Step 1 supplies the upper bound $b$ on $E_M$, so the lemma gives $H^r(Rj_*^{\mathrm{tot}}E_M)=0$ for $r>b+e$, where $Rj_*^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its unbounded total right derived functor. This is the same object as the bounded-below $Rj_*E_M$ of step 2 and as the unbounded K-injective $Rj_*E_M$ in the target of the projection morphism: K-injective resolutions exist for every complex of module sheaves, any two are chain-homotopy equivalent, and the bounded-below injective complex $I_M$ of step 2 is K-injective; every total right derived functor of $K(j_*)$ is computed on K-injective complexes, so $Rj_*^{\mathrm{tot}}(Q_VI_M)\cong Q_T(j_*I_M)$, and an additive functor carries a homotopy equivalence to a homotopy equivalence, so the K-injective formula of the projection morphism also gives $Q_T(j_*I_M)$. Hence $\mathcal H^r(Rj_*E_M)=0$ for $r>b+e$. Together with step 2 this puts $Rj_*E_M$ in $D^{[a,b+e]}$. For this finite $M$ the assumed projection morphism is an isomorphism, so $Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_T$ has the same cohomological interval. Only the projection isomorphisms assumed in the item have been used.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived (4)(c), with n=e+1; the projection isomorphism is an explicit hypothesis

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ and put $C=Q_{\bar t}\in D(A)$. The derived stalk is pullback to the point and commutes with derived tensor. The stalk of $M_T$ is $M$: the stated abelian-group identification is $A$-linear because it is natural for each scalar endomorphism of $M$. Stalks commute with cohomology. The cited cohomology assertion for abelian sheaves applies to module sheaves after forgetting scalar action: kernels, images and their quotient have the same underlying abelian sheaves and their induced scalar actions. Therefore step 3 gives
$$H^r(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)=0\qquad(r\notin[a,b+e])$$
for every finite $A$-module $M$.

Let $N$ be any $A$-module in the fixed universe. Its finitely generated submodules form a small directed poset: $0$ is one of them, and $N_1+N_2$ contains any pair. Every element lies in its cyclic submodule, so $N=\varinjlim N_i$. If $N_i$ has $m$ generators, it is a quotient of $A^m$, a finite set because $A$ is finite; thus each $N_i$ is a finite module, as required in step 4. Choose any complex of $A$-modules representing $C$. Apply the filtered-colimit derived-tensor theorem with its rings $R=A$ and its algebra also $A$, and with the complexes $N_i$ concentrated in degree zero. For every $r$ it identifies
$$H^r(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\cong\varinjlim_i H^r(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_i).$$
For $r\notin[a,b+e]$ the right side is zero by step 4. Hence the same vanishing holds for every module $N$. This argument takes filtered colimits only in the category of modules at a stalk; it needs no commutation of $Rj_*$ with colimits.

source.place: K-flat derived tensor and exact filtered colimits; specialization of lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor (source Tags 06Y6, 06YR)

proof.text:
Let $F$ be an arbitrary degree-zero $A_T$-module sheaf. At each geometric point $\bar t$ choose the module $N=F_{\bar t}$ in step 5. Derived pullback compatibility and the stalk-cohomology identity give
$$\mathcal H^r(Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F)_{\bar t}\cong H^r(Q_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F_{\bar t})=0\qquad(r\notin[a,b+e]).$$
These comparisons apply to ordinary unbounded derived tensor, so no boundedness of this tensor is being assumed. Geometric stalks detect isomorphisms of abelian etale sheaves: apply that assertion to the map from the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^r(Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F)$ to zero. Its stalk maps are isomorphisms, so the sheaf is zero, also as an $A_T$-module. Since $F$ was arbitrary, this is exactly Tor amplitude $[a,b+e]$ for $Rj_*L$.

proof_origin.place: Explicit stalk and filtered-union argument for the finite-constant-module Tor test, using Stacks-derived-functor and tensor lemmas.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-737e177b0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all 17 cited statements, the unit record, the current main-20261015 blueprint proof and the citer sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation step 3. The delivery has no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. Its hypotheses (Tor amplitude [a,b], uniform R^q j_* vanishing for q>e, projection isomorphism for finite constant M) are exactly what the citer supplies from its own steps 1–2 and from lem-sf-projection-finite-constant, and it keeps the arbitrary field. The coefficients are ordinary constant-A étale module sheaves throughout. Duplicate search over the DAG found no node stating the item: det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor needs k separably closed, and thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude needs k algebraically closed and constructible K. Checks by step: step 1 tests the hypothesis with M_V. Step 2 gets the lower bound from an injective representative that is zero below a (dplus-injective-representative (1), right-derived-plus-injective (2)). Step 3 applies lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound; all its hypotheses hold. Steps 4 and 6 use the stalk, monoidal-pullback, stalk-cohomology, constant-stalk and conservativity lemmas, at the same level of detail as the accepted det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor step 9. Step 5 applies lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor with R=A to the finitely generated submodules; this diagram is small and filtered, its colimit is N, and each submodule is finite. Edge cases checked: A=0, V or T empty, e=0, a=b, and Z/ell^2 coefficients, where finite modules can have infinite projective dimension. One repaired fault (C1/E5): step 3 silently identified three versions of the derived direct image — the upper-bound lemma's unbounded total RF, the bounded-below Rj_* of step 2 and the K-injective Rj_* in the projection morphism. The fixed step 3 shows all three equal Q(j_* I_M), citing prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist and lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived. Both nodes are added to uses and proof_deps and declared in split_report.tool_uses. I accept every declared tool use as a generic black box that does not replace the unit's route. No SGA is cited, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and the change creates no cycle.
